properties.name: Cinder Lake Crater Field
properties.reason: Craters blasted by USGS/NASA in July and October 1967 (47 then 96 more, 143 total) expressly to replicate the lunar surface for Apollo training. Crater Field #1 was designed to duplicate an area within Mare Tranquillitatis, from a Lunar Orbiter image of the Apollo 11 landing site.
properties.citation: USGS Astrogeology, Flagstaff; USGS data release doi:10.5066/P13W5FTZ

properties.name: Meteor Crater (Barringer)
properties.reason: Apollo crew geology training; best-preserved simple impact crater on Earth.
properties.citation: USGS Astrogeology Apollo field training programme

properties.name: Haughton Crater
properties.reason: Impact structure in a polar desert; NASA Haughton-Mars Project field campaigns for two decades. Analog for BOTH bodies, so both are recorded.
properties.citation: NASA Haughton-Mars Project, Devon Island, Nunavut

properties.name: Mauna Kea (PISCES test site)
properties.reason: NASA lunar rover field tests; source of lunar regolith simulant.
properties.citation: Pacific International Space Center for Exploration Systems (PISCES), Hawaii

properties.name: Moses Lake dune field
properties.reason: NASA lunar rover mobility testing in the sand dunes.
properties.citation: NASA lunar rover mobility field tests, Moses Lake, Washington

properties.name: Black Point Lava Flow
properties.reason: NASA Desert RATS (Research and Technology Studies) analog field campaigns.

properties.name: Askja caldera
properties.citation: Apollo astronaut geology field training, Iceland

properties.name: Ries Crater
